case.impact: TypeError thrown inside getNodeMailerPayload propagates through sendEmail()/await Promise.all(emailsToSend) so the whole batch fails; the handler catches it and logs only "Error sending AddGuestsEmails", so the organizer never learns guests were added and no partial emails are guaranteed sent.

case.refutation: If the handler always loads the booking with its attendees and rejects when none exist, and organizer.language is guaranteed by the CalendarEvent type construction upstream, then attendees[0] and this.t are safe and this is only a stylistic difference from base templates.

case.claim: Authorization gate at f6.R46-R48 combines the two team-role checks with && instead of ||, so isTeamAdminOrOwner is true only when the caller is simultaneously team admin AND owner of booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0; every non-owner/admin caller therefore depends solely on isOrganizer/isAttendee, and for personal events (teamId null -> 0) the admin check can never be satisfied.
case.trigger: A booking organizer, an attendee, or a team ADMIN (not OWNER) calls addGuests with valid new guest emails on a booking whose eventType.teamId is null/undefined (personal event).
case.impact: Legitimate collaborators who should be allowed to add guests are rejected with FORBIDDEN (f6.R54-R55), while the intended 'admin or owner' escalation path is effectively dead code; conversely nothing over-grants, so the observable regression is denied access rather than privilege escalation.
case.open_question: What is the intended authorization contract for addGuests: must any single sufficient condition (organizer OR attendee OR team admin OR team owner) grant access, and does the schema/route expose this mutation to teammates of the organizer?
case.refutation: Counter-evidence would be a documented product rule that only team owners may add guests and that organizers/attendees always cover the remaining cases; also if the intended semantics were strict (owner implies admin), && would be harmless except that it still fails for ADMIN-only members and for personal events where teamId ?? 0 matches no membership row. Delivered source contains no such spec, and addGuests.schema.ts was not delivered.

discovery_basis.discrepancy: Variable name and PR intent ('add guests via bookings') state admin-or-owner; the delivered predicate requires admin-and-owner, i.e. only owners pass it, since isTeamAdmin accepts ADMIN or OWNER but isTeamOwner requires role OWNER (f5.C264-C270, f5.C286-C292).

args.reason: The && operator and its dead-code consequence are confirmed in source (obs_3:e1, obs_10:e1; isTeamAdmin accepts ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner requires role OWNER per obs_4:e2/e3, so an ADMIN-only teammate yields false). However, the FORBIDDEN rejection for a legitimate collaborator (obs_10:e2) only violates a contract if the intended rule is disjunctive OR if some non-organizer/non-attendee teammate is a required beneficiary. No such obligation is delivered: addGuests.schema.ts and any route/test/spec were not provided, and confirm.handler.ts's analogous disjunction (obs_8:e1) is a different mutation's authorization predicate, not a bound requirement for addGuests. Per review scope I must not invent an expected obligation, so this witness stays unproven rather than refuted.
args.missing_fact: A bound specification of the addGuests authorization contract showing that a single sufficient condition (organizer OR attendee OR team admin OR team owner) must grant access — e.g. addGuests.schema.ts / _router.tsx route contract, an addGuests handler test asserting a team ADMIN (non-owner) or teammate caller is permitted, or a documented product rule — establishing that the && conjunction causes a concrete FORBIDDEN denial for an entitled caller.

case.impact: Team-member notifications mislabel the recipient context (organizer role/reply-to/rendered attendee), so replies and content do not correspond to the member who is being notified.
case.open_question: Is OrganizerAddGuestsEmail intended to be instantiated per team member at all, and does the base organizer-scheduled payload also ignore teamMember outside the `to` address?
case.refutation: If the product contract is that all copies show organizer-centric event details and only the recipient differs, or if the inherited base payload behaves identically for team members, the unused teamMember is intentional and not a defect.

case.claim: MultiEmailLazy re-exports next/dynamic's lazy component after erasing its type with `as unknown as typeof import("./MultiEmail").default`, so consumers get the eager component's static type while receiving a dynamically loaded component whose props/loading contract may differ.
case.trigger: A consumer imports MultiEmail from this module (e.g. the @calcom/ui barrel used by AddGuestsDialog at f4.C13) and passes props typed by the eager default export.
case.impact: Type checking validates against the eager signature, so any prop required by the dynamic wrapper (or any difference in the exported shape, such as ssr/loading options not configured here) is unchecked at compile time and can surface as a runtime prop error or missing fallback while the 40kb chunk loads.
case.open_question: Does ./MultiEmail's default export accept exactly the same props as the dynamic() wrapper, and does the barrel actually re-export this lazy file rather than the eager MultiEmail? Neither MultiEmail.tsx nor the ui index was delivered in this unit's source sides.
case.refutation: dynamic(() => import("./MultiEmail")) forwards all props to the resolved module's default export unchanged, so the cast is behavior-preserving for prop callers; the cast only silences TypeScript's own metadata about the wrapper, and no fallback/ssr option is required for correctness of the call site.

args.reason: The impact premise requires a prop/shape difference between the eager component and the dynamic wrapper. Observed source shows the exact opposite: MultiEmailLazy wraps ./MultiEmail itself (obs_3:e1), the barrel re-exports that lazy file as MultiEmail (obs_4:e1, obs_5:e3), the eager default export takes exactly MultiEmailProps {value, readOnly, label, setValue, placeholder?} (obs_8:e1, obs_5:e6) and the cast targets typeof import("./MultiEmail").default, so the static type is the identical props contract. The only real call site delivered passes precisely those props (obs_7:e3, obs_7:e4), and AddGuestsDialog imports MultiEmail from @calcom/ui (obs_0:e1). next/dynamic's returned component forwards all received props to the resolved module's default export unchanged, and no additional prop is required by the wrapper; ssr/fallback are optional configuration, not part of the props contract, so nothing "required by the dynamic wrapper" can go unchecked. Hence no compile-time-valid call can produce the alleged runtime prop error or missing-fallback failure for this witness.
args.statement: There is no differing props contract: the cast in MultiEmailLazy.tsx names the very module it dynamically loads (./MultiEmail), whose declared props interface MultiEmailProps is exactly what consumers such as AddGuestsDialog pass (label, value, readOnly, setValue), so type checking validates against the same shape the dynamic wrapper receives and forwards unchanged; no prop is added or required by dynamic() and none of the alleged unchecked-prop consequences can occur at this call site.

Direct reads disprove this: packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts contains `export default class AttendeeAddGuestsEmail extends AttendeeScheduledEmail`, whose inherited constructor (obs_10:e2) is `(calEvent: CalendarEvent, attendee: Person, showAttendees?)`. email-manager.ts imports that class as its default export (obs_9:e1), so the positional call at obs_9:e5 matches the class contract exactly, mirroring the sibling call `new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` in the same loop.
